Then came Harley and Bidgood, of ours, and as scoring was three aside, the home team won by 9 pts. to 12pts. The Eastleight team and Belgrave team shared (unequally!) all the awards, as the attached result shows.
Meanwhile Bidgood and Bentley were walking together and overhauling Field, Saunders had retired at shortly over half the distance and Bidgood caught Field at about 13 miles.
Jack Bidgood and Fred Bentley, two Police athletes who have already served our teams well in the past, did splendidly in finishing 15th and 10th respectively and both finished inside three hours.
As stated elsewhere, Green and Bentley have earned their Honours Badges; and it seems probable that by this time next year Rickards and Bidgood, and possibly A.

Our three heroes were Rickards, Bentley and Bidgood (they finished in this order in the Police long-distance championship) and to these names must be added that of a fourth, Pat Collins, who accompanied our men on a cycle and attended to their needs.
Bidgood, A.
Bidgood are no longer eligible. However, our remaining material has undoubted possibilities, and with conscientious training we should, at least, be among the placings.

Bidgood also showed that he intends carrying through with his improved form at the shorter distances. Adequate support was lacking for these two, however, and we finished a few points behind the Polytechnic Harriers in the scratch team race, in third position.

A moderate-paced start was made with Green, Rickards and Bentley in the lead, closely followed by Martin, Tookey, Bidgood and Harley. Before two miles had been covered, Martin had joined the leaders and in this order they proceeded along Parkside towards "The Green Man" Roehampton.
Rickards, Bentley, Martin and Bidgood have been the high-lights, but Rathbone, Willis, Boddington, Jarvis, Allen and White have also played their part.

With the New Year, we shall see them back in harness again, preparing for the 20 miles Championship, which has eluded us in recent years, despite some really fine walking on the part of our men. Bentley, Rickards, Bidgood, Martin, J.

Speechley was 10th and Bidgood 18th (both walking in Polytechnic colours); whilst Rutland and Wright finished together in 20th position. The last-named two and Treacher walked as members of Cadogan A.C.

From the start Jack Field cut out the pace, opening up a distance of 50 yards in the first mile from Bentley, Bidgood, Harley, Martin, Speechley and Rickards, all of whom appeared unconcerned at the pace set by the leader.

A little farther back were Bentley, Bidgood, Rickards and Joe King, all walking together. It was as early as this that Jock Martin was having a struggle, suffering from a touch of sunstroke, but manfully keeping going.
The next two, Bentley and Bidgood, seemed a little lazy, which means they are saving themselves for future events; and sixth came Bob Readman, who continues to improve and promises to do well.
Jack Bidgood also did well to finish fifth on his initial walk over this course.

The individual titles have also been won by our walkers, viz., Readman, Readman and Bidgood respectively. Mick Porter finished 5th in the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon Race on Easter Monday, which was run in very bad weather conditions.

At half distance we had a four point lead, with the “ A ” team scoring: Jack Rutland 2, Jack Bidgood 4, Jack Wakeley 9, Bert Clayton was close behind but was having an off day owing to a badly bruised heel.
